## Overview

The between/within split extended to **phonological memory** — word/nonword repetition, the ERB total `erbto` (#553): pooled across all four waves, how does phonological-memory level go with word-reading level, and does that association live between children or within a child's own movement? The transition counterpart is `lrp-rli-mech-090`; this model has no own-baseline term.

The exposure is a **raw score, not a bounded count**: its documented test maximum is recorded nowhere in the repository, so registering it as a bounded-count measure would fabricate a denominator (`lrp_rli_mech_090.py` records the reasoning). It therefore enters as the **standardised raw score** (`mechanism_is_covariate`), and `beta_between` / `beta_within` are per +1 SD of the observed ERB total — the raw-units SD is recorded beside the fit and quoted in the results. Child-wave rows whose `erbto` value was mean-imputed are **dropped** (`require_observed`): imputation plus an indicator is an adjuster policy, never acceptable for the exposure itself; the dropped count is reported. `erbto` is measured at every wave, so the within-child term is meaningful; it is also measured with error, which attenuates both slopes toward zero. The adjustment set mirrors `mech-090` minus the own baseline: hearing (with its missing-indicator), the t1 block-design ability proxy and linear age; `attend` is omitted as in `pl-001`.

## Model

$$
\eta = \alpha_{\text{wave}} + \beta_G G
  + \beta_{\text{between}}\bar z_i + \beta_{\text{within}}(z_{it} - \bar z_i)
  + \gamma_A z(A) + \sum_c \gamma_c z(c) + u_{\text{child}}
$$

where $z_{it}$ is the standardised **raw** ERB total at wave $t$ (not a logit) and
$\bar z_i$ its child mean. There is deliberately no own-baseline term.
